front_blocks.md: What is meant by the term **supply**?

back_blocks.md: Supply is the amount of a good or service that a producer is **willing and able to supply at a given price** in a given time period.

cards.front_md: What is meant by the term **supply**?
cards.back_md: Supply is the amount of a good or service that a producer is **willing and able to supply at a given price** in a given time period.

front_blocks.md: **True or False? **
A supply curve slopes downward.

back_blocks.md: **False. **
A supply curve slopes upwards as there is a **positive relationship** between the price and quantity supplied.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **market supply**.

back_blocks.md: Market supply is the **combination** of all the **individual producers' **supply for a good or service.

cards.front_md: Define the term **market supply**.
cards.back_md: Market supply is the **combination** of all the **individual producers' **supply for a good or service.

front_blocks.md: What is meant by the term **ceteris paribus**?

back_blocks.md: Ceteris paribus means that **all other variables remain constant** or unchanged.

cards.front_md: What is meant by the term **ceteris paribus**?
cards.back_md: Ceteris paribus means that **all other variables remain constant** or unchanged.

front_blocks.md: How is an **extension in quantity supplied** shown on a graph?

back_blocks.md: An extension in quantity supplied is shown by a **movement up the supply curve**.

cards.front_md: How is an **extension in quantity supplied** shown on a graph?
cards.back_md: An extension in quantity supplied is shown by a **movement up the supply curve**.

front_blocks.md: What does the term **individual supply** mean?

back_blocks.md: Individual supply represents the **supply of one producer** or firm.

cards.front_md: What does the term **individual supply** mean?
cards.back_md: Individual supply represents the **supply of one producer** or firm.

front_blocks.md: What is meant by the phrase **contraction in QS**.

back_blocks.md: A contraction in QS is a decrease in quantity supplied, shown by a **movement down the supply curve**.

cards.front_md: What is meant by the phrase **contraction in QS**.
cards.back_md: A contraction in QS is a decrease in quantity supplied, shown by a **movement down the supply curve**.

front_blocks.md: What does a **supply curve **show?

back_blocks.md: A supply curve is a graphical **representation of the price and quantity supplied** by producers.

cards.front_md: What does a **supply curve **show?
cards.back_md: A supply curve is a graphical **representation of the price and quantity supplied** by producers.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **profit-maximising** **producer**.

back_blocks.md: A profit-maximising producer behaves rationally and **wants to supply more as prices increase** in order to maximise profits.

cards.front_md: Define the term **profit-maximising** **producer**.
cards.back_md: A profit-maximising producer behaves rationally and **wants to supply more as prices increase** in order to maximise profits.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An increase in price causes the supply curve to shift right.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An increase in price causes a **movement to the right along the supply curve** (extension in quantity supplied).

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An increase in price causes the supply curve to shift right.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

An increase in price causes a **movement to the right along the supply curve** (extension in quantity supplied).

front_blocks.md: What are the **conditions of supply**?

back_blocks.md: Conditions of supply are factors that **shift the supply curve** to the left or right.

cards.front_md: What are the **conditions of supply**?
cards.back_md: Conditions of supply are factors that **shift the supply curve** to the left or right.

front_blocks.md: Define a **shift** in the supply curve.

back_blocks.md: A shift in the supply curve occurs when the **entire supply curve moves left or right** due to changes in one of the conditions of supply.

cards.front_md: Define a **shift** in the supply curve.
cards.back_md: A shift in the supply curve occurs when the **entire supply curve moves left or right** due to changes in one of the conditions of supply.

front_blocks.md: Which condition **causes supply to increase** when it decreases?

back_blocks.md: When **costs of production decrease**, supply will increase (the supply curve  shifts right).

cards.front_md: Which condition **causes supply to increase** when it decreases?
cards.back_md: When **costs of production decrease**, supply will increase (the supply curve  shifts right).

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The implementation of a **subsidy** will shift the supply curve to the left.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The implementation of a subsidy causes the supply curve to **shift right**. More is supplied at every price level.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The implementation of an indirect tax will shift the **demand curve** to the right.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The implementation of an indirect tax will shift the **supply curve** to the left. It is a** condition of supply**.

front_blocks.md: What is the impact of **new technology** on supply?

back_blocks.md: New technology** increases productivity and lowers costs** of production, so supply increases (shifts right).

cards.front_md: What is the impact of **new technology** on supply?
cards.back_md: New technology** increases productivity and lowers costs** of production, so supply increases (shifts right).

front_blocks.md: How does the **number of firms** in a market affect supply?

back_blocks.md: If the number of **firms increases, supply increases** (shifts right). If the number of **firms decreases, supply decreases **(shifts left).

cards.front_md: How does the **number of firms** in a market affect supply?
cards.back_md: If the number of **firms increases, supply increases** (shifts right). If the number of **firms decreases, supply decreases **(shifts left).

front_blocks.md: State the impact of **unusual weather events** on agricultural supply.

back_blocks.md: Weather events like **droughts cause supply shocks** and decrease supply in agricultural markets (supply shifts left) . Good weather increases supply (supply shifts right).

cards.front_md: State the impact of **unusual weather events** on agricultural supply.
cards.back_md: Weather events like **droughts cause supply shocks** and decrease supply in agricultural markets (supply shifts left) . Good weather increases supply (supply shifts right).

An increase in the firm's** labour costs** will increase the costs of production, leading to an increase in supply.

back_blocks.md: **False. **
An increase in the firm's** labour costs** will increase the costs of production, leading to a **decrease in supply **(supply curve shifts left).

The entry of new firms into a market decreases the supply of that good.
